defects.original:
The clean sheet came off the press so quietly that Elise thought for a moment the type had failed to touch it. She lifted the corner and saw the heading hold its edge against the pale paper. They had waited for the stock to dry, tightened the damaged bed, and rejected two trial sheets before attempting the public copy. There was no miracle in the impression, only the accumulation of small refusals to hurry. Elise carried the first clean correction to the market square. The square was filling with carts diverted from the broken bridge. A notice about the collapse hung beside a notice about the price of flour. Elise waited for a space on the public board large enough to hold the correction without covering either. Truth did not become more public by making another useful fact disappear.

[noncontiguous passage]

Miriam brought the sealed packet at last, opened in Jonas's presence before they left the shop. “I kept the packet because I was afraid of losing him,” Miriam said. The admission had cost her more than she had expected. She had hoped to defend her silence as loyalty and discovered that the same word had served Jonas as an excuse to deny his name. The packet contained Jonas’s mother’s apprenticeship request under the name Dunn. His mother had asked the printer to take him in under a name that would spare him the mill owner's enmity. Jonas had believed the packet was an accusation, but it contained his mother’s request for an apprenticeship. The request was a record of somebody trying to provide a future, not a proof that every choice made to protect him had been right. Miriam allowed Elise to copy the relevant passage while keeping the original in its envelope. They agreed the public correction needed the printing evidence; Jonas's family history belonged in it only where he chose to make it relevant.

[noncontiguous passage]

The correction consumed more stock than the urgent first notice had. They needed copies for the board, the council, the workers' room, and customers who would otherwise hear only the first rumour. The correction used three reams, leaving six. Elise wrote the final count in the delivery book and made clear which three reams had become finished copies. The seven from the first evening had gained two dry replacements before losing these three; the spoiled ream never re-entered the usable total. She thought of the cold attic where a travelling compositor had once shown her how to listen before striking a loose letter into place. Elise remembered an itinerant compositor teaching her to listen for a loose sort, at a time she could not date. She could remember the sound of his teaching better than the year or even the spelling of his name. Not every useful past fact came with a convenient date, and she left the date blank rather than supplying one that felt plausible.

[noncontiguous passage]

Miriam asked whether the shop window should be repainted to include Elise's new title. Elise said they could discuss it after the accounts were copied. There had been enough permanent decisions made under pressure. They returned to the narrow street, where Jonas had opened the cases and laid the proof envelope on the dry stone. He showed them the index before asking about supper. Nothing had been filed under scandal or vindication. There were dates, names, document numbers, and a short note directing the reader from Reed to Dunn. Elise touched the edge of the page with her unburned hand. The ordinary usefulness of that note seemed more durable than the praise she had received at the square. She asked him to make a second copy for the workers' room and went to light the small stove.
